blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine peso fell deeper into the 63-per-dollar territory on Wednesday, ahead of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) next rate-setting meeting. The local currency opened at 63.01 against the greenback before posting an intraday low of 63.3 as of 12:34 p.m., data from the Bankers Association of the Philippines showed. READ: Peso crashes further below 63:$1, a new record low That surpassed the previous record low of 63.23 set on Oct. 16. All 20 economists polled by the Inquirer expect the BSP to tighten monetary policy at the Monetary Board’s Oct. 22 meeting. Eighteen forecast a quarter-percentage-point increase, […]...
